title: Chat docs
intro: Chat is the chat of your own website and admin: a ready chat widget (or your own chat screens on the visitor API), AI replies with your own AI provider key, knowledge, tools, handoff to your staff, an inbox for your admin, leads, flows and reports. Every conversation, message, lead and knowledge entry is kept in your own database (Connections). Your website's tokens are in the Portal: open the website, then Install and tokens. The browser token is public and goes into your pages; the server token is secret and stays on your server.
localhost: Testing on your own computer: the browser token also works on pages served from localhost, *.localhost, 127.0.0.1 or [::1], on any port, over http or https. These pages use your website's real database, AI key and providers, so the chats made there are real. There is no test mode.
visitorApi: Headless: build your own chat screens on the visitor API with the browser token (Authorization: Bearer). A visitor is a guest or a signed-in Accounts user. The first message of a guest answers guestKey: keep it on the device (localStorage, not cookies or URLs) and send it with every request in the SS-Guest header. A signed-in visitor's Accounts sign-in goes in the SS-Sign-In header; when a device sends both, the guest's chats move to the account (merged by time into the account's own chat when it has one). GET /v1/chat answers the chat and its latest 50 messages; GET /v1/chat?after=<seq> the messages after a sequence number (the new ones), and GET /v1/chat?before=<seq>&limit=<1–50> older ones while earlier is true. Check for new messages from the browser with back-off, as the widget does: while the window is open and the tab visible every 10 s, half as often after 5 idle minutes, none after 15 idle minutes or while the tab is hidden, and every 3 s for 45 s while an AI reply is pending (aiPending); while the window is closed, GET /v1/chat/unread on load, on focus and every 5 minutes. POST /v1/chat/messages?wait=1 waits up to 20 s for the AI reply and answers it in replies; a slower reply is still being written (replyPending: true) and comes with the next checks. A reply still pending after 2 minutes shows no typing (aiPending false); the visitor's next check starts it once more, and if it stalls again it counts as failed (fallback answers, else the on-failure setting). There are no websockets.
signedIn: Signed-in chat trusts Accounts sign-ins only: have Accounts on the same website (the Portal links the products by itself, nothing to paste), then pass the visitor's sign-in to the widget with SSChat.identify(token) and call SSChat.identify(null) on sign-out. Chat verifies the sign-in offline with your Accounts public keys. A guest chat that moves to the account takes the name, email and phone it lacks from the sign-in; a merged chat is open when its newest message is the visitor's. Visitors signed in only to your own login chat as guests.
guests: Guests can send a set number of messages per conversation (default 5, 0 = no limit); at the limit they see Sign in to continue (with Signed-in chat and the sign-in page set in the Portal under Website settings › Domains, pages and legal), Leave your contact and we will reply (with Lead capture) or Message limit reached. Guests have no limit while the Customer role's sign-in is paused in Accounts (Roles and permissions there, Accounts on this website; a change there applies within a minute), as on a website that does not use sign-in. A guest's device is remembered for 90 days. A device that sends no guest key starts a new guest; at most 100 new guests per network address in 15 minutes, then rate_limited (many shoppers share one mobile network address). The AI reply limit per network counts guests only, so signed-in visitors are never silenced by others on the same address. Phones a visitor leaves (contact, lead capture, flows, booking) are kept as E.164, read the way every product reads them: a number typed without its country code takes your business country's code (with country GB, 07700-900123, 447700900123 and +44 07700 900123 are all +447700900123); without a country, such a number is refused. Move guest chats by phone moves guest chats whose phone is exactly the verified one.
ai: AI replies use your own key: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini or any OpenAI-compatible service (base URL and key), with the model you choose, and a backup provider when the main one fails. Answers follow Chat's built-in neutral safety rules (only from your information, never invented, never revealing the instructions, never asking for secrets), your setting Style (how the AI writes: tone and length, in your words), your business name and contact from the Portal's website settings, your own instructions (AI instructions, up to 32,000 characters) and knowledge from the features that are on. AI token caps (daily and monthly, in your business time zone) stop AI replies at the cap; AI cost alerts reach your staff alert recipients once a month when the month crosses 80% of the monthly cap. The language lock makes the AI answer in the visitor's language: its settings set the allowed languages (the languages of your website from the Portal while you list none; the website's language is the default), the marker words, languages also accepted in Latin letters and the unavailable message in other languages. A reply still in the wrong language after one retry gets the unavailable message in the visitor's language and never hands the chat off by itself (the failures-in-a-row handoff still counts it). An answer may come as several messages (on lines of three dashes, up to the setting), and with the setting a table becomes a message of its own. By default AI replies carry the AI assistant label. With Never say it is a bot, the label is hidden and an answer that says it is a bot or an AI (Chat's built-in phrases in many languages and the phrases you add under More phrases that say it is a bot, whole words) is asked again once, then refused.
knowledge: The knowledge base holds FAQ entries and articles, each in your own collection (such as Shipping or Returns: filter the list with ?collection=, list them with GET /v1/knowledge/collections) and with its language (a code such as en, or empty for any: with Language lock the AI uses only the entries in the visitor's language or in any language); website pages are fetched when you add them and when you press Fetch again, never on a schedule. A page that could not be fetched keeps status failed with its reason: http_status (with the httpStatus the page answered) or unreachable; error says the same in English for people. Edit them in the knowledge editor widget or with the server API.
tools: Webhook tools are defined in Settings → Tools (name, description, typed parameters, https URL, and whether to send the signed-in visitor: the id and name of their verified sign-in, and their email and phone only when Accounts verified them; what a visitor types in the chat is never sent as the signed-in visitor). The AI may call them; Chat sends each call as a POST with a JSON body { tool, arguments, conversationId, visitor? } and the header ss-chat-signature: t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<t>.<raw body>"> made with your tool signing secret (Settings → Tools: reveal, copy, regenerate). Calls time out after 8 seconds and at most 64 kB of the answer is read.
booking: Book-a-slot calls your own booking endpoint (Settings → Tools), signed like a tool call, with two requests: { action: "list_slots", from: "YYYY-MM-DD", to: "YYYY-MM-DD", timeZone, service? } answered with { slots: [{ id, start, end }] }, and { action: "book", slotId, service?, answers, conversationId } answered with { booked: true, reference? }. answers holds the visitor's answers to your booking questions by key (Settings → Tools, Booking questions, or PUT /v1/lists/booking_questions { value }, each { key, label, type: text, number, yes_no, choice, email or phone, required, options }; you start with name (required), email and phone); emails come in lower case and phones as +<country code><number>. service is the key of one of your booking services (PUT /v1/lists/booking_services { value }, each { key, name, description }), sent only when you have services; the AI then asks which one. With the setting A booking needs an email address or a phone number (on by default), the AI asks for one of them (a signed-in visitor's email counts and fills your first email question).
handoff: Handoff moves a chat to a person: the visitor asks (button or phrases), a keyword matches, the AI decides, or the AI fails a number of times in a row. The chat is flagged Waiting for a person and the AI stops until a staff member replies or hands the chat back to the AI (resuming the AI: Hand back to the AI in the inbox, or PUT /v1/conversations/<id>/ai with paused false). Outside your office hours the visitor is told when staff are back. Office hours are in your business time zone: weekly windows { day, start, end }, day 1 (Monday) to 7 (Sunday) and times as HH:MM with minutes (a closing time not after the opening runs past midnight; 24:00 is the end of the day), and dated exceptions { date: YYYY-MM-DD, name, hours: [{ start, end }] } that replace that day's hours (no hours = closed all day, for holidays). With no weekly windows, every day without an exception is open all day. A guest with no contact details is asked for them. Reassurance (after 5 minutes of waiting) and the queue position count from the latest handoff (waitingSince).
flows: Flows are short scripted step lists (message, question with buttons, collect a field, hand off, end), started by a page rule (the widget starts them when the chat opens on a matching page, or after the delay) or by a keyword in a visitor message. Path patterns start with /: an exact path, * = any characters inside one segment, ** = any segments (for example /products/**).
alerts: Staff alerts, AI cost alerts, transcripts and reply alerts are sent through Notifications: have Notifications on the same website (the Portal links the products by itself, nothing to paste). They go out with Chat's default words (US English) by email and SMS until you write your own templates in Notifications (Settings → Templates, where you can also switch a message off on a channel); WhatsApp has no default words, so it needs your WhatsApp template approved at Meta. Staff alerts and cost alerts go to the alert people you set once in the Portal (Website settings › Team and alerts: email addresses get email; phone numbers SMS, or WhatsApp when the team's phone channel says so; staff push if it is on) and, with the setting Also alert Accounts staff who can, to every unblocked Accounts user whose role may reply in the inbox (inbox.reply) or, with all_staff, may see the inbox (inbox.read) (Accounts token); new message and Chat needs you alerts also go to the assigned person; a message Notifications did not take is tried again on the website's next uses for up to a day. Transcripts are emails; without the token they answer notifications_not_connected. Reply alerts go when staff reply to a visitor who has not checked the chat for the away time (0: also while they are in it): with How often once (the default) one alert until they check again, with every_reply one for each staff reply while they are away; by the setting Channels, in order (email, SMS and WhatsApp; with none picked, the default, the channels switched on in Notifications: email, then SMS, then WhatsApp): the first channel the visitor has an address for (a phone for SMS and WhatsApp), and when Notifications does not take it there (that channel is off, has no template or is switched off for the message), the next one. To send no reply alerts, switch Reply alerts to visitors off. Alerts link to the setting Conversation page in your admin (adminUrl) with its values filled in, for example https://admin.example.com/inbox?conversation={conversationId}; the inbox widget opens the conversation named by ?conversation= in its page address. Staff alert values: visitor, name, preview (140 characters on one line), message (the visitor's latest message, up to 500 characters with its line breaks), phone (with the setting Alerts carry the visitor's phone), link, conversationId and business. A transcript carries the whole chat in {transcript}, a long value of up to 50,000 characters (your own template of chat.transcript uses it in the message, not the subject); a longer chat sends its latest messages after a line that says how many (widget text transcript.earlier).
attachments: Attachments go from the browser straight to your own S3-compatible storage with a short presigned PUT that fixes the type and size; Chat keeps only the object key. Allow your website's origin (and your admin's) in the bucket's CORS: methods PUT and GET, header content-type. Images browsers show (JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF, AVIF) show inline; videos (MP4, WebM, QuickTime) and audio such as voice notes (MP3, M4A, AAC, Ogg, WebM, WAV) play in the chat; HEIC and HEIF photos are downloads; PDFs, Word, Excel and text files are downloads. Visitors (with the setting Visitors may attach: everyone, or signed-in visitors only) send the file types of your list of upload types, each with its own largest size (Settings → Attachments, or PUT /v1/lists/upload_types { value }, each { type, maxMb } with maxMb 1–100; you start with JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF and PDF at 5 MB each). Staff send JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF and PDF files up to 10 MB. Attachment links are Chat's own (/v1/files/…): each use sends the browser on to a fresh 10-minute link in your storage, so the links of a chat left open keep working.
dataRights: Data rights: with Chat and Accounts on the same website, the Portal links them and Accounts reaches Chat. Export returns a person's conversations (with their messages and attachments' names) and leads; delete removes them, guest chats merged into the account included. Chat never deletes conversations because of their age; you delete them with DELETE /v1/conversations/<id>, or every one (your test chats before going live) with POST /v1/data/delete-all { scope: conversations, confirm: '<your domain>' } and the server token: their messages, attachments, guest records and staff alerts not sent yet go with them, leads stay; every lead with { scope: leads, confirm: '<your domain>' }; when the answer says more, call again.
activity: Activity log: every staff action through the widgets or the server API (reply, note, status, assignment, knowledge edits …) is kept in your database and copied to Accounts when it is on the website: who (with their role), what, the target with its label (the visitor's name, an entry's or saved reply's title), a short detail such as Status: open → resolved, and when — never message contents. Read it with GET /v1/activity (below).
kit: In Chat: the lists of GET and PUT /v1/lists/<list> are tools (Webhook tools), flows (Flows), custom_fields (Custom fields), page_rules (Page rules), fallback_answers (Fallback answers), redaction_patterns (Redaction patterns, each { name, pattern, replacement }), teams (Teams, each { name, members, languages, pages }), page_types (Page types, each { key, name, path, nudge }), office_hours (Office hours, each { day, start, end }), office_exceptions (Holidays and special hours, each { date, name, hours }), upload_types (Upload types, each { type, maxMb }), booking_questions (Booking questions, each { key, label, type, required, options }) and booking_services (Booking services, each { key, name, description }), tags, topics and priorities (each { key, name, description }), each the whole list in { value }, checked as in Settings. Conversations count with GET /v1/conversations/count and GET /v1/conversations/counts?by=status|waiting|guest|unread|topic|priority, with the list's own filters (status, waiting=1, visitor=guest|user, assigned=unassigned|me, tag, topic, priority, q); waiting, guest (the visitor is a guest) and unread (visitor messages no one on your staff opened) count as true and false. The inbox widget's twins are GET /v1/admin/conversations/count and /counts (inbox.read). Replies, status changes, assignment and knowledge edits made with the server token and the SS-Sign-In of a signed-in staff member carry that person's name (on the message, as staffId and name, and in the activity log with their role), add them to the staff list, and assigned=me means them; without a signed-in staff member a reply, status change or assignment is refused (403 needs_signed_in_staff). A visitor call from your server sends the guest's key in SS-Guest or the visitor's sign-in in SS-Sign-In, and SS-Visitor-IP: the AI reply limits per network count by that address.
shop: Shop assistant tools read your shop in Ecommerce: have Ecommerce on the same website (the Portal links the products by itself, nothing to paste). While Shop assistant is on, Settings → Shop tools chooses which tools the AI may use (search, deals, top products, my orders, track shipment, product cards). My orders and track shipment need a verified Accounts sign-in on that request.
install: Add the script to the pages of your website. The chat widget mounts itself; it renders nothing while Visitor chat is off, the product is stopped, or your database is not connected.
admin: Admin widgets run in your own admin with a ticket: Inbox (inbox.read to see conversations and set your presence, inbox.reply to reply and attach, inbox.manage for status, assignment, notes, saved replies, custom field values, tags, topic and priority, and max chats), Knowledge editor (knowledge.edit) and Reports (reports.read). The inbox setting Guest chats in the inbox shows every chat, guest chats only once handed to a person, or signed-in visitors' chats only (in the list, its counts and the unread badge); pausing the AI needs inbox.manage, or inbox.reply with the setting Pausing the AI needs. Staff may say why they pause the AI, and the inbox shows who paused it, when and why; Hand back to the AI resumes the AI in a chat waiting for a person. Tags, topics and priorities are your own lists (Settings → Inbox, or PUT /v1/lists/tags, /v1/lists/topics and /v1/lists/priorities { value }, each { key, name, description }; priorities start as Urgent, High, Normal and Low): staff give a conversation any tags, one topic and one priority in the inbox (PATCH /v1/conversations/<id> { tags, topic, priority } from your server, keys of your lists only), the list filters by them (tag, topic and priority), its counts group by topic and priority, and Reports count conversations by each. With the inbox setting The AI tags conversations (and AI replies on), the AI picks them from your lists only, never others, when a chat is handed to a person and when it is resolved, leaving what your staff already set; your descriptions tell it when each fits. Delete removes a conversation for good (inbox.manage, asked twice), a visitor's phone shows a Call link, and older messages load a page at a time. A chat can be assigned to anyone on the staff list: everyone the inbox has seen and, with the Accounts token, every Accounts user whose role may reply in the inbox; staff alerts reach the assigned person's email and, from Accounts, their phone; with Assign automatically set to first replier, an unassigned chat goes to the first member of staff who replies. Include the script without data-token, place the widgets and register your ticket function. The widget calls it at start and 1 minute before the ticket expires; your server checks the user's sign-in and role every time. SSChat.onUnread(callback) gives the unread count for your own menu; the server can read it with GET /v1/inbox/unread.
tickets: Your server asks for a ticket with the server token (never send the server token to a browser). The origin is the address of your admin page: any https origin, or a local one while testing. Tickets last 15 minutes and carry only the permissions of switched-on features.
api: Every API route answers JSON (204: no body); errors are RFC 9457 problems with a stable code. Lists are paged with cursor and limit. Routes of a feature that is off answer 403 feature_off. The reference below says what each call takes and answers.
cards: Product cards: the products search_catalog, get_product_details and get_top_products return (up to the setting Products per search: default 5, at most 12) show under the AI answer as cards with the image, the name linking to the product page, the price as the product page shows it (after the best live deal, with the earlier price struck through beside it; screen readers hear "was" and that price) and Add to cart. Add to cart dispatches the cancelable window event ss-ecommerce:add-to-cart with detail { productId, variantId, quantity: 1 }. Ecommerce's widget on the same page adds the item to its cart and calls preventDefault(); when no widget does, the card opens the product page instead. Your own cart can listen for the same event. Every word on a card is a widget text (Settings, Texts).
contextPanel: Context panel shop info: with Ecommerce on the website and a signed-in visitor, the inbox's context panel also shows the visitor's latest orders (number, status, total; the latest 5) and loyalty points, read from Ecommerce with the server token; for guests, or without the token, it shows nothing about the shop.
import: Import (server token only, feature Import): move staff, guests, conversations and their messages in from another system with ss-import, or with your own script on the import routes. POST /v1/import/<collection> takes NDJSON (application/x-ndjson, one record per line, at most 1,000 records or 4 MB per call) in Chat's own shapes: staff { id, name, email?, presence?, maxChats?, createdAt? }; guests { keyHash, id, expireAt?, createdAt? }, where keyHash is the SHA-256 (hex) of the old guest cookie value, so a guest's chats keep working through the store's own cookie sent as SS-Guest; conversations with their given ids (visitor, contact, status, waiting, AI pause, assignment, note, custom field values, summary, rating, the page it started on, unread counts, tags, topic and priority as keys of your lists, lastMessageAt, createdAt); and messages { id, conversationId, author, staffId?, name?, text, format?, internal?, attachment?, createdAt }, one record per message, after their conversations. Times are ISO 8601 with a zone. Each record is written by its key and replaced when it is there already, so a re-run gives exactly the source again; unknown fields and the tenant fields are refused by name, and text longer than Chat keeps is refused, never cut. ?dryRun=1 checks without writing. Then call POST /v1/import/finish (again with ?after=<next> while more is true): it numbers each imported conversation's messages 1..n by time and derives its counters, preview and read marks. POST /v1/import/<collection>/prune removes imported records the source no longer has (records made in Chat itself stay), and GET /v1/import/status answers the counts and the sums ss-import verify compares. An import sends nothing: no message, event, alert, AI call or activity copy.

build.visitor_chat: Add the widget script with your browser token to every page (copy it from Install and tokens in the Portal); the chat mounts itself, so there is nothing to place. Optionally use window.SSChat: setPage({ kind, productId, productName }) with kind the key of one of your page types (Settings → Proactive, Page types: product, category, deals and cart to start with, or your own; a page that names none is typed by the first path pattern it matches), open() and close(), and onUnread(callback) for your own badge. For your own chat screens instead, use the visitor API with the browser token: GET /v1/chat, POST /v1/chat/messages?wait=1 and GET /v1/chat/unread.
build.ai_replies: Nothing on your pages: the chat widget shows the AI replies. Enter your AI provider key once in the Portal (Website settings, Data and files: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini or an OpenAI-compatible service, with its key and model); Chat takes it from there and shows it as set in Connections. On your own chat screens, send with POST /v1/chat/messages?wait=1 and, while aiPending is true, check GET /v1/chat?after=<seq> every 3 seconds.
build.knowledge_base: Nothing on your pages: add FAQ entries and articles in the knowledge editor widget (Knowledge editor) or from your server with POST /v1/knowledge/entries. The AI answers from them.
build.webhook_tools: On your server, an https endpoint for each tool: Chat POSTs { tool, arguments, conversationId, visitor? } with the ss-chat-signature header. Check it with your tool signing secret (Settings → Tools; the check is in this guide) and answer with a 2xx (JSON or text) within 8 seconds, without redirects (at most 64 kB is read). Define the tools (name, description, typed parameters, address) in Settings → Tools or with PUT /v1/lists/tools { value }.
build.book_slot: On your server, a booking endpoint (https), signed like a tool call (check ss-chat-signature with your tool signing secret): it answers { action: "list_slots", from, to, timeZone, service? } with { slots: [{ id, start, end }] } and { action: "book", slotId, service?, answers: { <question key>: value }, conversationId } with { booked: true, reference? }. Put its address in Settings → Tools (Booking address), with your booking questions and services there (or PUT /v1/lists/booking_questions and /v1/lists/booking_services { value }).
build.shop_assistant: Have Ecommerce on the same website (the Portal links the products by itself, nothing to paste). The AI then answers questions using your store's catalog, deals, customer orders and tracking.
build.leads_flows: Nothing beyond the widget script: choose the lead fields and the consent text in Settings → Lead capture, and build flows in Settings → Flows or with PUT /v1/lists/flows { value }. The lead form shows at the guest limit and, outside office hours (Human handoff), to a guest who left no email or phone (on your own chat screens: leadOffered in the chat answer). Read leads from your server with GET /v1/leads (your staff see them in the inbox's Leads), and delete one with DELETE /v1/leads/<id> (Delete in the inbox, inbox.manage). On your own chat screens, use POST /v1/chat/leads, POST /v1/chat/flows/<flowId>/start and POST /v1/chat/flow.
build.inbox:
In your admin, place
with the widget script (without data-token) and SSChat.admin({ getTicket }). Your server checks the user's sign-in and role, then asks for a ticket with POST /v1/tickets (server token) carrying inbox.read, inbox.reply and inbox.manage as the role allows. Or work from your server with GET /v1/conversations and POST /v1/conversations//messages.
build.handoff: Nothing on your pages: the widget shows the Talk to a person button and the handoff notice (the widget text chat.handoffNotice, or none with the setting off). Set the phrases (in each language your visitors write in), and keywords in Settings → Handoff and office hours, with your weekly office hours and your holidays and special hours there (or PUT /v1/lists/office_hours and /v1/lists/office_exceptions { value }), and keep someone answering in the inbox. On your own chat screens, call POST /v1/chat/handoff when the visitor asks for a person.
build.moderation: Nothing on your pages: in Settings → Moderation, choose whether personal data is hidden (cards, IBANs, emails, phones, IPv4 and IPv6 addresses), your own redaction patterns (national or tax IDs, member numbers: a safe subset of regular expressions, checked when saved, that can never slow the chat down), your blocked terms, the link policy for AI answers and the phrases the AI must never reveal.
build.reports:
In your admin, place
with the widget script (without data-token) and SSChat.admin({ getTicket }), with tickets carrying reports.read; or read GET /v1/reports from your server. Reports also count conversations by your tags, topics and priorities.
build.import: Nothing on your pages. While Import is on (our admins switch it on for a move and off after it), run ss-import, or your own script with the server token: POST /v1/import/<collection> with NDJSON (staff, guests, conversations, then messages), then POST /v1/import/finish, and compare GET /v1/import/status.
